RHEUMATOLOGY — FOLLOW-UP
Date of service: 01/20/2026

Ms. Williams returns for SLE with class IV lupus nephritis, about six months from presentation. No rash since the fall, no joint pain or swelling, no mouth sores. Energy good. Nephrology in December: creatinine 0.9, UPCR 0.8 g/g, complements normal, anti-dsDNA lower.

Medications: mycophenolate mofetil 1000 mg twice daily; hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily; losartan 25 mg daily; prednisone, near the end of the taper.
Allergies: hydrochlorothiazide (photosensitivity); seasonal pollens.

Exam: BP 131/77, HR 86, weight 67.0 kg. No malar rash. No oral ulcers. Joints: full range, no synovitis. No edema.

Assessment: SLE, clinically quiet; renal parameters improving.

Plan:
1. Prednisone 5 mg daily, and hold at that dose.
2. Mycophenolate, hydroxychloroquine and losartan unchanged.
3. Return in 6 months.

reports.text: Portable AP chest. Lungs clear. No focal consolidation, effusion or pneumothorax. Heart size and mediastinal contours normal. Osseous structures intact.

documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT — PROVIDER NOTE
Arrival: 03/12/2026 18:05, brought in by friends.

HPI: 34 year old woman brought in for strange behavior after spending the day at an outdoor music festival. Friends say she was dancing wildly, kept saying she was overheating, and drank very little water. History is limited by agitation; obtained from friends and, later, the patient. Medications include sertraline and sumatriptan, and she takes an over-the-counter dextromethorphan cough syrup now and then for a long-standing throat irritation. She has lupus and is on immunosuppressive therapy. Friends deny alcohol or drugs at the festival; patient later confirms.

PMH: anxiety/OCD, migraine, asthma, SLE with kidney involvement.
Home medications (from our system): albuterol HFA as needed; fluticasone HFA 44 mcg 2 puffs twice daily; hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily.
Allergies: seasonal pollens; no known drug allergies.

Exam: T 39.7 C (103.5 F), HR 120, BP 168/94, RR 24, SpO2 97% RA.
Awake, agitated, intermittently combative. Pupils dilated. Profuse sweating. Bowel sounds increased. Neuro: inducible clonus at both ankles, hyperreflexia in both lower extremities, mild rigidity. Neck supple. No photophobia. Lungs clear. Heart tachycardic, regular. No rash.
Fingerstick glucose normal.

MDM: Clinical picture of serotonin toxicity (clonus, hyperreflexia, hyperthermia, agitation, mydriasis, diaphoresis) in a patient on sertraline and sumatriptan with dextromethorphan use, plus heat and dehydration. Because she is immunosuppressed and febrile, infection was evaluated as well: CBC, CMP, CK, urinalysis, blood and urine cultures and chest x-ray.

Results: CBC normal. CMP normal, creatinine 0.9. CK normal. Urinalysis bland. Chest x-ray clear. Cultures pending.

Treatment: active external cooling, IV fluids, IV benzodiazepine for agitation, cyproheptadine by mouth (loading dose, then scheduled). Sertraline and sumatriptan held. Dextromethorphan stopped.

Course: by 22:00 temperature 37.6, HR 94, calmer, clonus diminishing.

Diagnosis: serotonin syndrome.
Disposition: ED observation overnight.

Emergency Medicine

ED OBSERVATION — DISCHARGE NOTE
Observation 03/12/2026 to 03/13/2026

Diagnosis: serotonin syndrome.

Course: cooled, IV fluids, benzodiazepine and cyproheptadine. Temperature normal since midnight. Agitation resolved; alert and oriented, appropriate. Clonus resolved on morning exam; reflexes normal. Tolerating food and fluids. 10:30 vitals: T 36.8, HR 76, BP 120/76, RR 16, SpO2 99%.
Blood and urine cultures no growth so far; final results to PCP.

Instructions:
- Do NOT take dextromethorphan (in many cough and cold products).
- Hold sertraline and sumatriptan until reviewed by your PCP and psychiatrist.
- Hydrate, rest, avoid heat today.
- Follow up with PCP within 1 week.
- Return for fever, confusion, muscle stiffness or twitching.

OUTPATIENT PSYCHIATRY — FOLLOW-UP
Date of service: 03/24/2026

34 year old woman with GAD and OCD, on sertraline 100 mg daily until 3/12/2026, when she was treated in the ED for serotonin syndrome in the setting of sertraline, sumatriptan and over-the-counter dextromethorphan, plus heat exposure. Sertraline has been held since. Dextromethorphan is now on her allergy list, and limited sumatriptan is allowed.

Off sertraline for 12 days. Physically recovered. No compulsions. No suicidal ideation. She would like to resume treatment.
Allergies: dextromethorphan (serotonin syndrome); hydrochlorothiazide (photosensitivity); seasonal pollens.

Mental status: cooperative, mildly anxious, logical, no suicidal ideation.

Plan:
1. Restart sertraline at 50 mg daily.
2. Reviewed warning signs of serotonin toxicity; no dextromethorphan; sumatriptan sparingly.
3. Return in about 8 weeks to consider returning to 100 mg.

OUTPATIENT PSYCHIATRY — FOLLOW-UP
Date of service: 05/19/2026

Eight weeks back on sertraline 50 mg after the March serotonin syndrome. No recurrence: no fever, tremor, twitching or agitation. No dextromethorphan. Sumatriptan used twice for migraine, without problems. She feels the 50 mg dose is not holding her worry as well as 100 mg did. No compulsions. No suicidal ideation.

Mental status: calm, cooperative, logical, mildly anxious.

Plan:
1. Increase sertraline to 100 mg daily, her previous dose.
2. Continue to avoid dextromethorphan and other serotonergic over-the-counter products.
3. Return in 3 months.

NEPHROLOGY CLINIC
Date of service: 06/16/2026

Re: Fatou Williams, 34
Diagnosis: SLE, lupus nephritis ISN/RPS class IV (biopsy 7/1/2025)

About a year from presentation. Feels well. No swelling, no rash. ED visit in March for serotonin syndrome, unrelated to the kidneys; creatinine there 0.9.

Current therapy: prednisone 5 mg daily; mycophenolate mofetil 1000 mg twice daily; hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily; losartan 25 mg daily.
Allergies: dextromethorphan; hydrochlorothiazide (photosensitivity); seasonal pollens.

Vitals: BP 112/79, HR 73, weight 66.3 kg. No edema.

Labs 6/16: creatinine 0.8 mg/dL; albumin 4.1 g/dL; urine protein/creatinine ratio 0.3 g/g; C3 and C4 normal; urine sediment bland. CBC normal.

Assessment: complete renal response.

Plan: regimen unchanged: prednisone 5 mg, mycophenolate 1000 mg twice daily, hydroxychloroquine 200 mg, losartan 25 mg. Labs and visit in 6 months.
